# Policy-KB bijection audit — catering_order_desk / task 0

Scope: product **catering**, 53 published documents; the difficulty's `catering.extended.yaml`
(12 base policies, 4 extended policies, 6 variants, 55 parameters), `task_tools.py`, and
`tasks/0.json`. Entry conditions cited from the brief: the policy-side verdict PASSED at round 3;
`check_docs.py` on `catering` returned `DOCS OK` (53 docs, roles policy 12 / facet 14 / baseline 4 /
hub 4 / factor 19, 136 required quantitative keys, 4 task tools, 2 prerequisite edges);
`check_traceability.py` on `tasks/catering_order_desk` returned `TRACEABILITY OK`. The auditor ran
neither, and is independent of the render agent and of the policy-side auditor.

The blind answer for this task was frozen to
`audits/runtime_context/catering_order_desk/0.md` before any of the above was opened.

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the catering prose was traced back. Findings:

**B1 — `catering_alongside_the_wider_dining_programme_96d2ac61`, section "The recorded position by
service level". KB-BIJECTION RED.**

> "The concession for catering produced out of the client's own cafe kitchen is recorded against
> every service level of the Corporate Catering Service Agreement except the Executive Hospitality
> Catering Account, and the guest count at which an order passes to the banquet book is the largest
> guest count printed against the service level."

*Source.* The second half is faithful: `escalate_to_banquet_above_guests: =max_headcount` on every
variant. The first half renders the per-variant parameter `delivery_fee_waived_with_cafe`
(True on every level, False on the Executive Hospitality Catering Account) — that is, the
**delivery-fee** waiver, the parameter of the two clauses this same document prints as "no longer
in force".

*What the rendering changed.* The rendering drops "delivery fee" and names the parameter "the
concession for catering produced out of the client's own cafe kitchen". That is the business name of
the concession the extended policy actually operates — `overwrite[1].replaced_by` reads "The
concession for an order produced out of the client's own cafe kitchen is taken on the service charge
rather than on the delivery charge" — and that concession is the live factor
`kitchen_service_concession`, published in
`service_charge_where_the_clients_own_cafe_kitchen_serves_fef64bdb`. That factor's ladder has
**no service-level condition**: its three tiers turn only on whether the cafe contract at the
delivery site stands open and whether its service model takes catering out of that kitchen.

*Consequence.* The corpus publishes, in a second document, a per-service-level condition on the same
named concession that the factor's ladder does not carry. On any Executive Hospitality Catering
Account whose client holds an open cafe contract taking catering out of that kitchen, the factor
document selects "no service charge is raised" while this sentence says the concession is not
recorded against that level at all — the whole 22.0 per cent. A difference in wording is benign only
if it cannot move a tier; this one can.

*Not triggered by either task in this difficulty.* Task 0's agreement is an Attended Buffet Account,
against which the concession is recorded; task 1's agreement is an Executive Hospitality Catering
Account but its client holds no cafe contract at all, and the invoicing policy is outside task 1's
charter scope. The scan is nonetheless of the whole domain, so it is recorded.

*Policy-side component, recorded and not used to change this verdict.* The source keeps
`delivery_fee_waived_with_cafe` as a live per-variant parameter of a base policy both of whose
clauses using it are retired, and says nowhere that it is spent or that it now qualifies the
service-charge concession. That leaves the render with a parameter it must carry and no clause to
carry it under.

**B2 — two ladders published under the business name "volume discount". Recorded as a translation
risk; not a red light.**

`standing_and_volume_discount_schedule_2712a0b9` Part B states: "The volume discount ladder printed
against each service level maps trailing ninety-day catering spend, in USD, to an extra discount
percentage", with per-level figures (1.0 / 2.0 / 3.0 per cent on the Attended Buffet Account).
`volume_step_on_catering_spend_4b595156` states a different ladder for what looks like the same
thing (0.75 / 1.5 / 2.5 points, on the counting window and the invoiced-order count). The live base
sentence in `invoicing_basis_for_catering_orders_5d0c3c9f` — "The standing discount and the volume
discount are added together rather than the better of the two being taken" — bridges either of them
into the total discount rate.

Both have structured sources: Part B is the `volume_discount_ladder` parameter, rendered in the
words of its own schema description; the factor document is the extended ladder. And the clause that
used Part B operatively is printed verbatim as "no longer in force" in the same document that
carries the bridge sentence. So this is not the retired surface stated as a rule in force, and I do
not record it as `KB-BIJECTION RED`. It is recorded because it is a live risk a reader can fall into:
taking Part B as the operative ladder on this task's world gives trailing ninety-day spend of
2100.00, no step, a total discount rate of 3.00 rather than 3.75, and the pair 6534.99 / 36550.00
instead of 6167.65 / 20943.77.

**B3 — intermediate rounding. Policy-side note.**

`amount_invoiced_for_a_served_catering_order_67753a0c` §6 and
`closing_figure_of_a_catering_agreement_9cf47192` both state the assembly as "added in that order and
rounded to two decimal places only at the end". The source-layer `compute` blocks round several
intermediates (`discounted_food`, `service_charge`, `rush_amount`; `shortfall_due`, `late_charge`),
and the GT trace does the same. The KB is faithful to the source's own `rule` text, which also says
"rounded to two decimal places only at the end", so the mismatch is internal to the source. On this
task's world the two paths agree to the cent. Recorded, not scored against the documents.

**No additions found.** A pattern scan over all 53 documents for cross-problem operational guidance
("first call …", "before the desk …", "then call/unlock/raise/register", "refer to", "see also"),
for procedure/checklist/roadmap/step-list language, and for confirmation, review, notification or
escalation obligations the source does not impose, returned nothing. A scan for seeded world state
written in as policy fact — the caller names, the client account codes `CA-22417` / `CA-22853`, the
site codes `CS-244` / `CS-271`, the order references `CO-7xxxxx`, the balances 4530 / 17812.5, the
order values 5860 / 6400 / 5700, and any literal `2025-` or `2026-` date — returned nothing. Every
illustration in the corpus is introduced as hypothetical.

- **B1** — `docs/catering/catering_alongside_the_wider_dining_programme_96d2ac61.json`, section
  "The recorded position by service level", first clause. A per-variant parameter of a retired
  delivery-fee clause is rendered under the name of the live service-charge concession, adding a
  service-level condition that the ladder of `kitchen_service_concession` — published in
  `docs/catering/service_charge_where_the_clients_own_cafe_kitchen_serves_fef64bdb.json` — does not
  carry, and that can move that factor's tier on an Executive Hospitality Catering Account.

Recorded alongside it, not reaching a red light: **B2** (two volume ladders live in the corpus under
one business name) and **B3** (the assembly sentence does not describe the source's intermediate
roundings).

Everything else corresponds losslessly: all 12 retired clauses verbatim and marked retired, all
non-retired base sentences carried at the same strength, all 4 baselines complete with their
defaults, all 19 factor ladders carried tier by tier with every threshold in figures and every
compound condition whole, all 55 per-variant parameters rendered with the right figures against the
right variant, both task-tool contracts exact, and the prerequisite sentence verbatim on the blocked
side and nowhere else.

### Round-1 item B1 — closed

Round 1 recorded: the per-variant parameter `delivery_fee_waived_with_cafe` was rendered as "The
concession for catering produced out of the client's own cafe kitchen … except the Executive
Hospitality Catering Account", under its own heading "The recorded position by service level" — the
business name of the *live* service-charge concession, whose ladder has no service-level condition.

The heading and that sentence are gone. In their place, inside the retirement note for the two
clauses the parameter actually backs:

> "This clause is likewise **no longer in force**. The waiver of the **delivery fee** that these two
> retired clauses turned on stays recorded against every service level of the Corporate Catering
> Service Agreement except the Executive Hospitality Catering Account."

Judged against the three things round 2 was asked to check:

- **Does the atom survive?** Yes. The source still carries `delivery_fee_waived_with_cafe` on all
  six variants, and it still has a bearing document. Dropping it would have traded one red light for
  another — a source atom with no home — so keeping it was right.
- **Does it now sit where a reader takes it as governing what it governs?** Yes. It names the
  **delivery fee** explicitly, and it is anchored to "these two retired clauses", which are the two
  delivery-fee clauses quoted immediately above it. The document no longer contains the word
  "service charge" anywhere, so there is nothing for the parameter to attach itself to.
- **Can it still be read as qualifying the live concession?** No. The round-1 sentence named no
  charge, which is why it floated onto the live service-charge concession; the replacement names one.
  I re-checked the live concession document: `service_charge_where_the_clients_own_cafe_kitchen_
  serves_fef64bdb` still states three tiers turning only on the cafe contract's standing and its
  service model, with no service-level condition, and no other document now states one.

One residual I record without raising it: "stays recorded … against every service level" is carrying
the sense "is a figure of a clause no longer in force", and it does so on the strength of the
retirement stated in the first half of the same sentence. It could be read as the waiver still
operating on the delivery fee. I judge the risk small and not worth a red light — the retirement is
stated first and in bold, the verb is "recorded" rather than "raised" or "applies", and the live
delivery charge is governed by `delivery_charge_where_a_site_sits_on_a_standing_round_c3b5e0e3`,
which states its own three tiers with no cafe condition at all. Compared with round 1, the sentence
can no longer move any factor's tier, which was the whole of the finding.

**The moved second half.** "The guest count at which an order passes to the banquet book is the
largest guest count printed against the catering service level, on every service level of the
agreement" now sits under "Large parties and the banquet book", immediately after the live base
clause it elaborates. Its source is unchanged (`escalate_to_banquet_above_guests: =max_headcount` on
all six variants). The move did not change that clause's meaning: the clause already referred to
"the largest guest count printed against the catering service level", and the sentence states the
parameter behind that reference. The added "on every service level of the agreement" is a coverage
statement, true of all six variants, not a new condition.

**B1: CLOSED.**

### The three declines — judged on their merits

**Intermediate rounding (my B3): decline accepted, not re-raised against the render.** The source
carries two statements about where rounding falls — the `rule` and `baseline.rule` say "rounded to
two decimal places only at the end", while the `compute` block rounds `discounted_food`,
`service_charge`, `rush_amount`, `shortfall_due` and `late_charge`. The render skill's contract is
that the computation document carries the **rule**; writing the compute's roundings into the prose
would be rendering a different artifact and asserting a precision the published rule does not state.
The renderer is right that this is not its to close. I re-verified this round that both paths give
20943.77 on this task's world. **Re-raised at the source layer instead**, where it belongs: the
charter's own `rule` text and its `compute` disagree, and only the source layer can reconcile them.

**Notice-band ordering (my C2): decline accepted, not re-raised against the render.** The three-way
notice sentence in `cancellation_notice_and_charges_2873d9a3` belongs to the un-retired base rule
`catering_cancellation_charges`, and this skill's own rule is explicit — base law is rendered as the
source has it, and a base sentence that states an order is a policy-side note, never a KB verdict.
I recorded it as a policy-side note in round 1 and it stays one. **Standing policy-side note:** on a
Drop-Off Catering Account where notice is given on the service day through the named account
manager, the counted notice is 24 hours and reaches that level's 24 free-cancellation hours, and the
base sentence and `percentage_the_notice_given_yields_b980fca9` then disagree. Neither task in this
difficulty reaches that world.

**The two volume ladders (my B2): decline accepted, not re-raised against the render.** I declined
to make this a red light in round 1 for the same reason the renderer now gives, and I hold to it:
Part B of `standing_and_volume_discount_schedule_2712a0b9` renders the `volume_discount_ladder`
parameter in the words of its own schema description, the parameter is live in the source on all six
variants, and the clause that used it operatively is printed verbatim as "no longer in force" in
`invoicing_basis_for_catering_orders_5d0c3c9f`. A render that deleted it would create an unborne
source atom. **Standing policy-side note:** the source keeps a per-variant parameter whose only
operative clause is retired, and says nowhere that it is spent — the same shape as B1, which is why
B1's fix had to keep the atom too.
